profile.disclosure_policy: Confirmed directly on AWS own Global Infrastructure page (aws.amazon.com/about-aws/global-infrastructure/regions_az/): AWS does not publish specific street addresses or per-building technical specifications (square footage, power capacity in MW) for its data centers, as a matter of stated security and operational policy. AWS states each Region consists of a minimum of three isolated, physically separate Availability Zones, each with independent power, cooling, and physical security, but does not break this down to individual facility addresses. This session confirmed this disclosure policy directly rather than assuming it, and applies this finding to AWS records that otherwise have no facility specific address, square footage, planned capacity, or critical_it_mw on file. This is a company wide policy finding, not a statement that no such facility exists at this location.

reading.body:
This is an Amazon Web Services data center in the Fort Worth metropolitan area, part of a region that has become active for hyperscale development in recent years. AWS does not publish specific power capacity, square footage, or technical specifications for individual buildings as stated company policy, so this facility's contribution to AI infrastructure cannot be measured from published sources. The facility's existence and location are confirmed, but no capacity figure can be derived or stated here.

Fort Worth and Dallas-Fort Worth rank among active hyperscale markets in Texas, with reported AWS expansion into the region driven by available land, power infrastructure, and business regulatory environment. Texas has 133 mapped data center facilities and 468.41 MW of published capacity across 18 facilities. This AWS site has no published capacity on record, placing it outside the ranked set of facilities with disclosed megawattage in the state.

The unpublished status of this facility means it cannot be assessed as a discrete constraint on AI scaling or compute availability. If capacity exists here, it is operationally significant to AWS but not visible in the public record this site maintains. Operators choosing to publish specifications enable measurement of regional compute density and grid pressure; AWS's policy choice to withhold facility-level detail leaves this location's role in the AI infrastructure buildout undocumented in the metrics that matter to grid planning.
